choices.content: Whether one event occurs does not change the probability of the other
The two events cannot occur simultaneously
The two events must occur simultaneously
The sum of the probabilities is 1

solutions.explanation: For events \(A\) and \(B\), independence means that whether one event occurs does not change the probability of the other. Its defining probability relation is \(P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)\). An empty intersection describes mutual exclusivity. Thus the correct choice is A.
solutions.title: Meaning of independence
